data.text:
PNP: MENDIOLA LABOR DAY PROTEST GENERALLY PEACEFUL

WATCH: Philippine National Police spokesperson PMaj Philipp Ines says no untoward incidents were reported during the Labor Day rally of workers’ groups along Mendiola Street on Friday, May 1.

Authorities estimate around 3,000 protesters joined the march. Despite not being a designated freedom park, Ines noted that rallyists were still able to hold their program peacefully and air their grievances.

Protests began early in parts of Manila and wrapped up past 10 a.m.

data.text:
SITWASYON SA KALAW AVENUE

Inilabas ng Manila Police District (MPD) ang litrato ng nanuntok na raliyista sa mga nakabarikadang pulis sa bahagi ng Kalaw Avenue sa Maynila ngayong Biyernes, May 1.

Sumugod kasi rito ang mga nagra-rally at nagtangkang lumapit sa U.S. Embassy.

Giit ng MPD, pinairal nila ang maximum tolerance. I via Mon Gualvez

#MSNews | The Philippine National Police (PNP) confirmed on Friday that seven of its personnel were injured while securing a Labor Day protest along Kalaw Avenue, Ermita, Manila during the Labor Day demonstration, after some rally participants turned aggressive and physically confronted police personnel.

Initial reports indicated that officers under Civil Disturbance Management (CDM) formation were observing maximum tolerance and professionalism when some demonstrators suddenly engaged the police line, resulting in physical assault and theft of personal belongings.

All injured personnel are currently confined at the PNP General Hospital for medical evaluation and management. One personnel is under close observation pending results of CT Scan, while the rest continue to receive appropriate medical care.

PNP Chief, General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., emphasized that restraint must not be taken as weakness:

“My directive is clear—maximum tolerance, yes, but we will never allow our police to be harmed or insulted while they are performing their duties. It is unacceptable," he said. | via Vince Lopez
